title: Populate verified import and export dependency edges

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as confidence-bearing JavaScript and TypeScript module edges with honest partial-resolution posture.

provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 output; exact reviewed specimen not identified

feedback.verbatim: Missing the 'Edges' (Import/Export Graph): You have successfully mapped the nodes (files and symbols) and the hierarchical parent-child containment (parent=F...). However, you are missing the lateral edges: the dependency graph. Idea: Introduce an @edges or @graph block. If warp.mjs imports cli.mjs, explicitly mapping that import -> export edge gives the agent the ability to execute blast-radius analysis before altering a signature.
feedback.normalized_claim: Populate trustworthy lateral import/export relationships so an agent can reason about dependency direction and signature-change blast radius.

current_behavior: MKTCTX/3 already defines an @edges block and machine-manifest edge records.
The current generator emits status=unavailable with reason=module resolution not implemented instead of guessing edges.
ContextEdge can represent from-file, to-file, kind, and optional symbols, but no analyzer currently populates it.

proposal.summary: Add analyzer-backed import/export resolution that populates the existing @edges structure with explicit completeness and provenance semantics.
candidate_changes: Determine whether Graft exposes resolved module relationships that can be consumed without reimplementing language resolution.
Define file-level import edges first, then add imported and exported symbol IDs only when resolution proves them.
Emit complete, partial, or unavailable status with per-language and per-edge reasons.
Represent unresolved, dynamic, type-only, re-export, and wildcard imports without pretending they are ordinary runtime edges.
non_goals: Do not infer dependency edges from matching names alone.
Do not claim a complete graph when unsupported languages or dynamic resolution remain.

questions: Which languages and module systems must the first resolver support?
Can Graft provide resolved edges and symbol identities, or is a separate resolver required?
Should import, export, re-export, call, inheritance, and reference edges share one grammar or distinct typed blocks?
How should path aliases, package exports, generated modules, and TS-to-JS extension rewriting be represented?
risks: False edges are more harmful than an explicit unavailable graph because they produce incorrect blast-radius claims.
Language-specific resolution can make the supposedly portable format depend on build configuration and environment state.
A dense symbol graph may consume more tokens than it saves unless filtered or summarized.
evidence_needed: Inventory of the installed Graft API's graph and resolution capabilities.
Cross-language fixtures for direct imports, re-exports, aliases, dynamic imports, and unresolved modules.
Model evaluation measuring signature-change and blast-radius accuracy with and without edges.
Token-cost measurements for file-level versus symbol-level graphs.
